I will keep my land in the usual Quzhou pattern: winter wheat first, then summer maize on the same fields. That is what I know best, it fits our local weather and water conditions, and it gives me grain from both seasons instead of taking a bigger risk on a crop I do not know as well. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because I want steadier emergence and yield. I will prepare the land with rotary tillage before wheat and again lightly after wheat harvest for maize so I can move quickly between crops. For fertilizer, I will give wheat a bit more total nutrient because it stays in the field longer, and I will push nitrogen more on maize because that crop responds strongly when summer rain comes. I will irrigate wheat several times if water allows, especially at key stages, while maize will rely more on summer rainfall with only limited extra irrigation. I will spray only when needed, but I still expect a few pesticide applications in each crop because I do not want weeds, aphids, armyworms, or common diseases cutting yield. My goal is stable production and manageable fieldwork, not gambling on a fancy plan.
